audit.whatIsWrong: Three content strings treat Tumble as an invisibility escape available from level 2: spikes[0].text 'before Tumble's invis is a real escape', early 'save the root for when she Tumbles, because once her invis is up she's gone', and wants.foe[0] 'Tumble into invis to dodge your Solar Snare'.
audit.why: Tumble grants no invisibility on its own. Riot's text for Tumble is only 'Vayne tumbles, maneuvering to carefully place her next shot. Her next attack deals bonus damage' — its single derived flag is autoReset. Invisibility during Tumble is granted by Final Hour (R), which is a level 6 ability with a 100s cooldown at rank 1. So for the entire stretch the entry describes — levels 2 through 5, the exact window it correctly identifies as Mel's takeover — the invisibility it warns about cannot happen. The cost is concrete: the entry tells Mel to hold Solar Snare in reserve for a vanishing act that does not exist, when the content layer's own plan is to root Vayne on every step-up.
audit.corrected: Tumble is a plain dash with an auto-attack reset until level 6. Invisibility on Tumble exists only while Final Hour (R) is active.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vayne.json (Q Tumble flags: autoReset; description has no stealth)
champ-data/_kits/vayne.json (R Final Hour: 'gains increased Attack Damage, Invisibility during Tumble, reduced Tumble cooldown'; cd 100/85/70)

audit.whatIsWrong: Condemn is the tracked, matchup-defining ability in both layers — it is the focus letter, it is in the win condition, the enemy win condition, the wave note and four don'ts — and neither layer ever states that it is a projectile Rebuttal can reflect.
audit.why: Condemn carries the projectile flag and Rebuttal reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker. The content layer calls Condemn-into-a-wall 'a death sentence with no dash to escape it', and the full layer's tldr instead spends its one headline telling the player what her W does NOT do ('His dash goes through your reflect'). Mel has a direct answer to the ability this entry is built around, and the entry uses its most prominent line to describe a non-interaction instead.
audit.corrected: Condemn is a projectile — Rebuttal is the answer to it. Hold W for the crossbow bolt, not for chip.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vayne.json (E Condemn flags: projectile, knockup, hardCC, terrain)
champ-data/_kits/mel.json (W Rebuttal reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t all tell the player to wait for Condemn's downtime and none of them says how long it is.
audit.why: Condemn is 20/18/16/14/12 — twenty seconds at rank 1, which is one of the longest windows in this slice and by far the most exploitable thing about the matchup. Mel's Solar Snare is 11s over the same period, so she gets roughly two roots per Condemn. That ratio is the whole reason the early game belongs to her, and stating it turns 'wait for its downtime' from a platitude into a plan.
audit.corrected: Condemn is 20s at rank 1 against an 11s Solar Snare — you get two roots per Condemn.

audit.whatIsWrong: Silver Bolts is described only as 'itemized Silver Bolts shred your squishy frame in true damage'. The three-hit trigger and, more importantly, what counts toward it, are never stated.
audit.why: Riot's text is 'The third consecutive attack or ability against the same target deals a percentage of the target's max health as bonus true damage'. Abilities count, which means Condemn is one of the three — so the real burst pattern is two autos plus Condemn, not three autos. A Mel player who thinks she has three autos of margin before the true damage lands is off by a full attack, and against a champion she cannot out-trade that is the difference between stepping back in time and dying. The missing-interactions file also flags Tumble as an auto-reset burst tell, which pairs with this: the reset is how Vayne compresses those hits.
audit.corrected: Silver Bolts procs on the third consecutive attack OR ability on the same target — Condemn counts as one of the three.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vayne.json (W Silver Bolts: 'The third consecutive attack or ability against the same target')

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d, breakdown.trading and report[3].t say Rebuttal is 'gone for twenty seconds'.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26. The coincidence is unlucky here — Condemn genuinely is 20s at rank 1, so the entry states the wrong ability's number for Mel's W and omits it for Vayne's E. Correcting it also fixes the trade maths: spending W on chip means eating the next Condemn AND the one after it.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal is gone 38s at rank 1 — nearly two Condemns.

audit.why: 56.25% over 16 games, EVEN at 5.5/10, and both level charts broadly agree that Mel owns the early and middle and Vayne takes 2+ items. This is the most internally consistent entry in my slice — full.phases actually varies (Mel, Mel, Mel, Skill, Skill, Skill, Vayne) instead of being bulk-filled, and it tracks content.win closely. No rating edit.

The spike timeline is right and specific: Mel's window is level 2 through first item, Vayne's is two crit items. 'Silver Bolts deal percent-max-HP true damage' in content.late is confirmed by Riot's text, so the scaling warning is accurate as written.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vayne.json (W Silver Bolts: 'a percentage of the target's max health as bonus true damage')

notes: Cleanest entry in my slice on ratings — 56.25% over 16 games, EVEN 5.5/10, and full.phases actually tracks content.win here (Mel, Mel, Mel, Skill, Skill, Skill, Vayne) rather than being bulk-filled like the Sylas and Urgot entries. I proposed no rating changes. Two real errors. First, three content strings sell Tumble as an invisibility escape from level 2; Tumble only turns invisible while Final Hour (R) is active, so for the entire level 2-5 window the entry itself calls Mel's takeover, the escape it warns about cannot happen. Second, Condemn is the ability both layers are built around and neither says it is a projectile Rebuttal reflects — the full layer's headline was spent instead on the non-interaction 'His dash goes through your reflect'. PRONOUNS: the full layer refers to Vayne as 'his' and 'him' throughout (tldr, tradeGood, dosFull[1].t, dontsFull[1].t, dontsFull[2].t, breakdown.trading, report[3].t, enemyWin's phrasing). The content layer correctly uses 'her'. I fixed it in the strings I was already editing for factual reasons — 'his' to 'her' is length-neutral so these are safe — but I did not open extra edits purely for pronouns. Remaining offenders: dontsFull[1].t 'Trade inside his effective range with E down', dontsFull[2].t 'Greed stacks when his all-in is loaded', dosFull[2].t 'Kite with the W move speed out of his reach'. All three are 3-for-3 character swaps if you want them. NOT ASSERTED: I say Rebuttal reflects Condemn because Condemn carries the projectile flag, but I did not claim the reflect negates the knockback or that a reflected bolt can wall-stun Vayne. Displacement-versus-reflect behaviour is not answerable from the kit files. Confirmed correct and left alone: content.late's 'Silver Bolts deal percent-max-HP true damage' matches Riot's text exactly, and dosFull[2].t 'Kite with the W move speed' is right — Rebuttal does grant movement speed. The suspectNames hit on spikes[0] ('Solar Snare's', distance 2) is a false positive from the possessive apostrophe.
